title: Equality of condensed model and adic geometric global Frobenius
statement:
Fix $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, $E=\mathbf Q_\ell\subset\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme $Y_0$, $Y=Y_0\times_{k_0}k$, and $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Let $\Phi:Y\to Y$ be the $k$-linear base change of the $q$-power Frobenius of $Y_0$. Let $E_Y$ have the canonical geometric Weil structure [def-weil-constant-weil-structure], and set $C_E=R\Gamma_c(Y,E_Y)$ [def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology]. Let $F_E:C_E\to C_E$ be exactly the compactly supported geometric Frobenius of [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], including its specified cohomology-transport arrow. Construct $(K,\phi)$ over $\underline\Omega=\operatorname{Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj}(\ell)$ and the isomorphism $\sigma_Y:Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}K\xrightarrow{\sim}\rho_{E,s}(C_E)$ exactly as in [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge], where $\rho_{E,s}$ is [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace]. For $m\ge1$, let $G_m$ be the globalOperator of $\operatorname{weilCompactCohomology}(K,\phi_m)$, formed with the specific $\operatorname{compactCohomologyFrobeniusComparison}$ and the iterated model Weil map as in [nt-assume-trace-formula]. Then the specified comparison conjugates the actual operators:
$$\sigma_Y\circ G_m=\rho_{E,s}(F_E^m)\circ\sigma_Y.$$
In particular, under its cohomology comparison, $H^i(G_m)$ is the scalar extension of the $m$-th power of the geometric Frobenius on $H_c^i(Y,E)$, for every $i$. This is an equality for the stated model-Frobenius comparison, with the geometric convention (on $H_c^2(\mathbf A^1_k,E)$ the eigenvalue is $q^m$), not an assertion that an unspecified object isomorphism is Frobenius-equivariant. The assertion makes no use of a trace-formula identity or Poincare duality.

proof.text: Use the normalized constant integral object $M=\widehat{\mathbf Z}_{\ell,Y}[0]$ and its geometric Weil map $u:Lg_Y^*M\xrightarrow{\sim}M$. Its reductions are $M_n=(\mathbf Z_\ell/\ell^n)_Y[0]$, with the quotient transitions, by [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum] and [lem-weil-constant-coefficient-objects-constructible]. Each $M_n$ has Tor amplitude $[0,0]$: tensoring the coefficient unit with any module returns that module in degree zero, by multiplication with inverse $z\mapsto1\otimes z$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. The reductions of $u$ are the normalized geometric maps $u_n$; their scheme maps are $\psi_n=u_n\kappa_n$. Apply [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] with this actual $u$ and $N=0$, so its rational map is exactly the constant geometric Weil structure, with no denominator or scalar rescaling.

source.place: Clauses (2)–(3): normalized coefficient maps and their global realization

proof.text:
For $m\geq1$ the same rational-model theorem gives the actual finite-level iterates $\psi_{n,m}=u_n^{[m]}\kappa_n^{(m)}$ and graph operators $T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$. The comparison in [prop-trf-graph-frobenius-operator] uses exactly this canonical $\kappa^{(m)}$, and gives
$$T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})=R\Gamma_c(Y,u_n^{[m]})\,g_{\gamma,c}^{m,*}.$$
Its hypotheses hold by Step 1 and separated finite type of $Y_0$. In particular the scheme map is the model Frobenius fixing $k$, whereas $g_Y$ is the geometric Galois map; they have not been equated as scheme morphisms. Clause (3) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] identifies the whole-tower realization of these graph maps with
$$U_m=R\Gamma_c(Y,u^{[m]})\,V_{m,M},$$
where $V_{m,M}$ is the integral transport along $g_Y^m$. This uses its assertion about realization, not faithfulness of separate reduction functors.

source.place: Clauses (2)–(3): normalized coefficient maps and their global realization

proof.text:
Here is the power calculation before rationalization. Write $H=R\Gamma_c(Y,-)$, $P_m=L(g_Y^m)^*$ and $c_m:P_1P_m\simeq P_{m+1}$. Define $u^{[m]}$ by composing $m$ pulled-back copies of $u$, so $u^{[m+1]}c_m=uP_1(u^{[m]})$. The whole-system recurrence and naturality in [lem-trf-integral-compact-transport-recurrence] give
$$\begin{aligned}
U_{m+1}&=H(u^{[m+1]})H(c_m)V_{1,P_mM}V_{m,M}\\
&=H(u)H(P_1u^{[m]})V_{1,P_mM}V_{m,M}\\
&=H(u)V_{1,M}H(u^{[m]})V_{m,M}=U_1U_m.
\end{aligned}$$
Thus $U_m=U_1^m$ by induction starting at $m=1$. By the rational-model theorem with $N=0$, and its explicit identification at $m=1$ with [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius], $U_1[1/\ell]=F_E$ including the point transport. Hence $U_m[1/\ell]=F_E^m$. Rationalization preserves this finite composition.

source.place: Clauses (2)–(3): normalized coefficient maps and their global realization

proof.text:
Let $h=\Phi^m$ and $P_\Omega=Ra_{Y!}^{\mathrm{cond}}$. Put $\Theta_m=\operatorname{compactCohomologyFrobeniusComparison}$ at $K$, with the identity pullback on $s$ removed. By the definition of the Weil compact-support pushforward in [nt-assume-trace-formula], $G_m=P_\Omega(\phi_m)\Theta_m$. The implementation-normalization lemma [lem-zl-model-compact-comparison-unit] gives
$$G_m=P_\Omega(\phi_m)d^{\mathrm{cond}}_{h,K}.$$
This computes the exact comparison specified in the question. It does not substitute a chosen equivariant structure for the one in the interface.

source.place: Global graph operator; concrete module-object comparison is isolated as a new implementation-normalization obligation

proof.text:
Apply [lem-zl-proper-unit-condensed-realization] to $M$ and $h=\Phi^m$. These maps are proper: model Frobenius is finite by [lem-trf-scheme-frobenius-finite-radicial]; it is therefore proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and finite composition of proper maps is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. The reductions of $M$ satisfy the required Tor condition by Step 1. Completed pullback of this coefficient unit is again the coefficient unit: at each quotient the tensor-unit map sends $a\otimes b$ to $ab$, and the maps commute with quotient reductions; completion uses this same unit tower. Hence the two rational compact cohomology complexes are bounded finite-dimensional, as required by [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge]. Use its specified coefficient realization $K=\mathcal R_Y(M)$ and comparison $\sigma_Y=b_M$. With $M'=Lh^*_{\mathrm{comp}}M$, the new proper-unit lemma yields
$$b_{M'}P_\Omega(c_{h,M}^{-1})d^{\mathrm{cond}}_{h,K}
=\rho_{E,s}(D_{h,M,E})\sigma_Y,$$
where $D_{h,M,E}=\operatorname{Fib}_s(R\lim d_{h,\bullet})[1/\ell]$. The assertion is on whole towers and includes the point comparison.

source.place: 6.7.6–6.7.7 and 6.8.14–6.8.15; proper-unit coherence is explicitly the statement-only prerequisite cited here

proof.text:
Let $v_m:M'\to M$ be the integral model coefficient map obtained by the normalized coefficient-unit pullback isomorphism, with its prescribed iterates. By [lem-zl-assumed-trace-determinant-bridge] this is the map whose realization gives $\phi_m$; the pullback comparison is $c_{h,M}$, so $\phi_m=\mathcal R_Y(v_m)c_{h,M}^{-1}$. Its finite reductions are $\psi_{n,m}$ of Steps 1–2: the initial maps agree by [lem-zl-constant-weil-datum], and the iterates agree by induction using the same pullback compositors preserved by [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization]. Naturality of $b$ in [lem-zl-proper-unit-condensed-realization], followed by its unit equality from Step 5, now gives
$$\begin{aligned}
\sigma_YG_m
&=b_MP_\Omega(\mathcal R_Y(v_m))P_\Omega(c_{h,M}^{-1})d^{\mathrm{cond}}_{h,K}\\
&=\rho_{E,s}(C(v_m))b_{M'}P_\Omega(c_{h,M}^{-1})d^{\mathrm{cond}}_{h,K}\\
&=\rho_{E,s}(C(v_m)D_{h,M,E})\sigma_Y.
\end{aligned}$$
Here $C(v_m)$ means the rationalized compact-support map on coefficient complexes, and all intermediate sources are those displayed in Step 5.

source.place: Clauses (2)–(3): normalized coefficient maps and their global realization

proof.text:
At finite level the definition of $d_{h,n}$ in [lem-zl-proper-unit-condensed-realization] and [prop-trf-graph-operator] identify $P_n(\psi_{n,m})d_{h,n}$ with $T_{c_m}(\psi_{n,m})$. The whole-system naturality in that realization lemma says the corresponding integral composite is the realization of these same graph maps. Clause (3) of [prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model] identifies it with $U_m$. Therefore $C(v_m)D_{h,M,E}=U_m[1/\ell]=F_E^m$ by Step 3. Substituting this equality in Step 6 proves exactly
$$\sigma_YG_m=\rho_{E,s}(F_E^m)\sigma_Y.$$
The argument uses the finite graph comparison, its coherent integral realization, and the two specified proper-unit comparisons. No trace-formula equality or Poincare duality enters.

source.place: Clauses (2)–(3): normalized coefficient maps and their global realization

proof.text: Apply $H^i$ to the equality just proved. The cohomology comparison for the finite-matrix functor in [lem-zl-condensed-point-supertrace] is natural in chain maps: its matrices are the same scalar-extended matrices. Hence under $H^i(\sigma_Y)$ the map $H^i(G_m)$ is $H^i(F_E^m)\otimes_E\Omega$, which equals $H^i(F_E)^m\otimes_E\Omega$ because cohomology preserves composition. This is the claimed statement for every integer $i$, including degrees with zero cohomology. The convention is the geometric one throughout, fixed by [def-weil-global-geometric-frobenius] and the canonical $\kappa$ in the finite graph theorem; no inverse of that operator has been introduced.
